paragraphs: Westminster City Council is one of eight west London councils that recruit foster carers together through Foster with West London, alongside Brent, Ealing, Hammersmith and Fulham, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hounslow, and Kensington and Chelsea. The partnership is funded by the Department for Education and acts as a single point of contact for anyone in the area who is thinking about fostering, whichever of the eight councils they would like to foster for.

In practice this means your first conversation is with the shared hub rather than with a single borough. The hub handles enquiries, applications and the early stages of recruitment, and you can get in touch online, by phone or by video call. When you are asked which council you want to foster for, you can name Westminster, and once you have applied your application is taken on and assessed by that council's own fostering service. The hub says it keeps supporting people as they go through the process, with updates from professionals at each stage, and that this support carries on after the hand-over to the council.

Foster with West London also runs information sessions where you can meet foster carers and social workers and ask what fostering is really like before you commit to anything. It is a sensible first step if you live in Westminster and are weighing up whether the timing is right for you and your household.

The services shown above also include independent agencies that work in Westminster. Speak to Foster with West London and to two or three of the agencies, and compare the training, out-of-hours support and payments each offers for the children you could care for before you decide. Nearby boroughs in the same partnership, such as Kensington and Chelsea and Hammersmith and Fulham, have their own pages on this site.
